column1: # docs/inspection.md §18.3 count ratchet — see tools/count-ratchet.sh
# id<TAB>count.  A count may FALL freely; raising one is a deliberate act.
# 2026-10-01: 8.1.8 +2 and 10.7 +3 are CORPUS GROWTH, not drift — both are the
# pre-existing style of bin/qwen-memory-index-patch.sh (two >120-char lines, three
# `echo … >&2` sites), a script that lived only as an unversioned ~/.local/bin copy
# until it was tracked here.  Deliberate re-baseline for ONE newly added file.
# (Restored by hand after `--update`: the tool rewrites the file without comments.)
# 2026-10-01 (second re-baseline, same day): every rise below is the PRE-EXISTING
# style of code that became TRACKED, not new drift — six files moved in from loose
# ~/.local/bin copies (autotune-rows.sh, bench-rows.sh, gpu-passthrough-check.sh,
# so, xo, serve) plus bin/heavy-job, which is new.  Corpus 81 -> 88 files.
# Not counted here: bin/heavy-job's own single `[ … ]`, which was changed to
# `[[ … ]]` instead — the counter's ask — when it was written.
# 2026-10-01 (third re-baseline, same day): CORPUS GROWTH, not drift.  Two files were
# tracked in from loose ~/.local/bin copies — bin/qwen-guard-patch.sh and
# bin/qwen-guard-selfheal.sh — with their own edits kept comment-only, so every counter
# they raise is pre-existing style.  Contributions measured by running the counters over

# d1df5ce9 tracked ONE new shell file, bin/qwen-guard-selfheal.sh; measured with this
# tool's own counters over that file alone it raises 4.2.4 +1 and 6.7 +4.  Corpus
# 89 -> 90.  The third block above counted bin/qwen-guard-patch.sh as tracked too, but
# it is still UNTRACKED, so its 8.1.8 +18 / 9.5 +2 / 10.4 +1 / 10.7 +10 are absent from

# 8.1.8's 272 also carries +2 from another lane's uncommitted scripts/09d-oc-agents.sh

# committed).  Deliberate re-baseline: corpus growth, not drift.
